profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the engineering enablement team and the research tooling team at a large developer-platform company that is preparing an internal pilot based on the paper 'Empirical Software Engineering: From Discipline to Interdiscipline.' The company wants to turn the paper into a cross-functional reading-and-annotation exercise for staff engineers, UX researchers, and engineering managers, then collect structured reflections for a later internal methods workshop. The immediate coordination need is to align on the interface between the two workstreams: the research tooling team will set up the annotation workspace and export pipeline, while the engineering enablement team will draft the facilitation guide, participant instructions, and final summary deck. The agenda is to confirm what 'the pilot package' includes, what artifact will be handed off on Friday, which version of the paper and annotation schema everyone is using, and how progress/status should be interpreted for the launch. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on deliverables, handoff timing, and ownership of shared artifacts so both teams can proceed without further meetings this week.

members.name: Nina Park
members.expertise: Developer education, internal workshops, technical communication, rollout coordination
members.background: Nina previously led onboarding and learning programs for a cloud infrastructure group and now runs internal engineering learning initiatives that translate research papers into practical workshop formats for product and platform teams.
members.private_state: Nina wants this pilot to look turnkey to directors by Friday, avoid another round of review, and keep the facilitation burden low for volunteer discussion leads.
hidden_assumptions: The 'pilot package' means the facilitator guide, participant instructions, slide deck, and a stable link to the annotation workspace; raw export files are supporting materials, not part of the core package.

When people say the 'current paper,' they mean the cleaned internal reading copy in Confluence with company formatting and a one-page framing note, because that is what facilitators will actually distribute.
A status of 'ready' means usable by a facilitator without manual cleanup or interpretation, even if some backend instrumentation or metadata polish is still pending.
The shared annotation schema is owned by the research tooling team once the initial fields were suggested, so she expects them to finalize field names and export shape.
A Friday handoff for internal training materials conventionally means by end of business Pacific Time so facilitators can review before the weekend.

members.name: Arjun Mehta
members.expertise: Study infrastructure, annotation systems, data pipelines, internal experiment operations
members.background: Arjun builds lightweight research platforms for internal studies and has recently been supporting mixed-methods initiatives across engineering, design, and organizational research teams.
members.private_state: Arjun wants to minimize custom work, reuse an existing annotation/export pipeline, and avoid becoming the long-term owner of workshop content decisions.
hidden_assumptions: The 'pilot package' means the configured annotation workspace, schema JSON, export template, and setup notes; facilitation materials are separate downstream assets owned by enablement.
When people refer to the 'current paper,' they mean the source PDF uploaded into the annotation platform, because exports and anchor offsets depend on that exact file.
A status of 'ready' means the workspace is available, the schema validates, and one dry-run export works; facilitator polish or participant-facing wording is outside that status.
The annotation schema content was drafted by enablement, so field definitions and naming decisions remain Nina's team's responsibility even if he implements them.
A Friday handoff in cross-team tooling work means by 23:59 UTC unless someone specifies local business hours, because deployment and export jobs are timestamped globally.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the pilot package
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both talk about delivering 'the pilot package' on Friday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Nina means a facilitator-ready bundle: guide, participant instructions, summary deck draft, and a usable annotation link, with the tool setup as one component inside the package.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Arjun means the technical handoff bundle: configured workspace, schema file, export template, and setup notes, with workshop-facing materials outside the package.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In coordination meetings, 'package' sounds like a shared umbrella term and each person's role makes their interpretation feel obviously included, so neither expects the other to mean materially different boundaries.

misalignment_points.topic: Which paper version is the current paper
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to 'the current paper' and 'the paper everyone will annotate.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Nina is thinking of the internally reformatted Confluence reading copy with section headers normalized and a framing note prepended for workshop participants.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Arjun is thinking of the original uploaded PDF used by the annotation tool, because annotation anchors and exports are tied to its page and character offsets.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both versions have the same title and nearly identical content, so casual references to 'the paper' seem fully sufficient; the operational consequences only appear later when anchors or page references differ.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on wanting the workspace and materials to be 'ready' by Friday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Nina believes 'ready' means a volunteer facilitator can run the pilot with no extra interpretation, including polished instructions and a clean export example embedded in the guide.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Arjun believes 'ready' means the system technically functions for the pilot: workspace live, schema valid, permissions set, and export tested once.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both criteria are plausibly associated with readiness, and in a cooperative meeting each hears the other as endorsing the same practical goal without spelling out the threshold.

misalignment_points.topic: Who finalizes the shared annotation schema
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'lock the schema today' so downstream work can proceed.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Nina assumes Arjun will clean up field names, normalize categories, and make implementation-minded choices before locking it, because his team owns the tooling artifact.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Arjun assumes Nina will confirm final wording and category boundaries, and he will simply implement whatever is already decided, because content semantics belong to enablement.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both genuinely agree the schema should be locked and neither sees ownership of the micro-decisions as controversial; the phrase hides different assumptions about who performs the last mile of finalization.
